# Vibhaṅga-mūlaṭīkā (Tika Abh02t)

**ID:** Tika Abh02t
**Section:** Tīkā Vibhaṅga-mūlaṭīkā (tika-abh02)
**Collection:** Tika-Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Vibhaṅga-mūlaṭīkā
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Vibhaṅga-mūlaṭīkā* (also recorded under the titles *Paramatthapakāsanī II*, *Līnattha-jotikā II*, and *Līnatthajotanā II*) is the principal subcommentary (*ṭīkā* or *mūlaṭīkā*) on the *Sammohavinodanī*, Ācariya Buddhaghosa's commentary on the canonical Abhidhamma treatise *Vibhaṅga* [Gal 2003; Nyanatusita 2008; Ronkin 2005]. It forms the second major part of the tripartite *Abhidhamma-mūlaṭīkā* authored by Ācariya Ānanda [Nyanaponika and Bodhi 2012; Nyanatusita 2008]. Ānanda's provenance and period are debated in modern scholarship: he is variously described as a South Indian master active in the late fifth or early sixth century, as an Indian mainland master according to the *Gandhavaṃsa*, as an elder of Sri Lanka, or dated by Walpola Rahula to around the tenth or eleventh century [Bodhi 1999; Lamotte 1988; Nyanaponika and Bodhi 2012; Rahula 1956]. The purpose of the work is to elucidate obscure terms and difficult doctrines in the commentary and to provide further analytical clarity on the canonical text [Nyanaponika and Bodhi 2012]. The text was subsequently commented upon in an *Anuṭīkā* (secondary subcommentary) by Ānanda's pupil Dhammapāla [Bodhi 1999; Nyanaponika and Bodhi 2012]. In modern scholarship, it is studied via editions such as the Burmese-script Chaṭṭhasaṅgāyana edition, and cited on specific technical points of Abhidhamma analysis, such as its gloss identifying the factors of absorption (*jhānaṅga*) in the Khandhavibhaṅga as "strength-givers" (*bala-dāyakā*) [Nyanaponika and Bodhi 2012].

Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects extensive Pali-internal sharing, registering over 51,000 matches with 424 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its largest textual overlap is with the *Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā* (over 327,000 shared characters in part two and over 57,000 in part one), followed by the *Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-ṭīkā*, the underlying *Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā*, the *Dīghanikāye Mahāvaggaṭīkā*, and the canonical *Paṭiccasamuppādavibhaṅga* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches scoring 10 or above are identified [DharmaNexus].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā (Dutiyo bhāgo) (Anya E0104n) (§373_0–376_14 ↔ §864_4–868_13); Majjhimanikāye Mūlapaṇṇāsa-ṭīkā (Tika S0201t) (§1351_0–1353_11 ↔ §1494_0–1496_11); Vibhaṅga-aṭṭhakathā (Atk Abh02a) (§1502_7–1502_10 ↔ §604_2–604_6); Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā (Tika Abh08t) (§1578_0–1578_30 ↔ §1972_0–1974_1); Dīghanikāye Mahāvaggaṭīkā (Tika S0102t) (§574_0–580_1 ↔ §1228_3–1233_3); Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi (Tika Abh09t) (§316_4–316_6 ↔ §1294_1–1294_4); Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0517a) (§2002_1–2002_6 ↔ §2274_10–2275_1); Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā (Paṭhamo bhāgo) (Anya E0103n) (§1889_0–1895_1 ↔ §114_0–115_7)

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 1999] Bhikkhu Bodhi (ed.), Comprehensive Manual of Abhidhamma (1999) — Authorship of the Mūlaṭīkā by Ānanda and the Anuṭīkā by Dhammapāla.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Machine-calculated Pali-internal text reuse and cross-language alignment data.
- [Gal 2003] Noa Gal, Metaphysics of Experience: From the Buddha’s Teaching to the Abhidhamma (2003) — Identification of the text as the Vibhaṅga subcommentary.
- [Lamotte 1988] Étienne Lamotte, History of Indian Buddhism (1988 [1958]) — Geographical provenance of Ānanda according to the Gandhavaṃsa.
- [Nyanaponika and Bodhi 2012] Nyanaponika Thera and Bhikkhu Bodhi, Abhidhamma Studies: Buddhist Explorations of Consciousness and Time (2012) — Context on the Mūlaṭīkā's role, authorship, date, editions, and doctrinal gloss on jhāna factors.
- [Nyanatusita 2008] Bhikkhu Nyanatusita, Reference Table of Pali Literature (2008) — Alternative titles Paramatthapakāsanī II and Līnattha-jotikā II.
- [Rahula 1956] Walpola Rahula, History of Buddhism in Ceylon: Anuradhapura Period (1956) — Discussion of ṭīkā literature and proposed 10th–11th century dating for Ānanda's Mūlaṭīkā.
- [Ronkin 2005] Noa Ronkin, Early Buddhist Metaphysics (2005) — Identification of the text as the Vibhaṅga subcommentary.
